title: Review aid: packing ceilings of 14 open complex kappa claims (stacked on #1240; no new kappa)
body:
**Stacked on #1240** (it reuses `research/complex-local-word-ceiling/ceiling.py`). Once #1240 lands, this PR retargets to `main`. No new κ. **No claim is accepted, rejected or reviewed by this PR.**

**Card:** `complex-new-helper-inventory` (complex-mechanisms, chooser seed `9fe32a6efcf929bf30bb65fb781eb095`, base `dadfea6e`). Scope is refined to the card's "reject routes without headroom" step, applied to inventories already in the review queue. This answers #1240's first open question.

## What it does
30 open PRs state κ above the selected 0.001672660197076918. For each, I searched one package for:
- a complex profile whose κ equals the title κ;
- live stock W and call count N;
- an idle histogram consistent with the coverage law `mass = 72W + 64N`.

**14 claims** qualify. They are pinned by head, path and Git blob in `SNAPSHOT.json`; `rebind.py --fetch` re-reads every blob. Each profile splits into local word plus idle, and #1240's exact relaxation caps any repacking of that word.

## Result
All 14 obey the coverage law at 896/9 families per call, and every endpoint lies below its own cap. They use **9 distinct local words**:

| Word family | Caps on κ | Claims | Headroom left |
|---|---|---|---|
| selected-type (W1, W2 = selected, W4, W5) | 0.0016872026–**0.0016873148** | #1124 #1129 #1130 #1131 #1152 #1157 | 0.77–0.86% |
| #1148 joint-entrance (W3, W6–W9) | 0.0016836800–0.0016843188 | #1148 #1178 #1193 #1195 #1196 #1204 #1225 #1239 | 0.47–0.52% |

- **No repacking of any covered word passes κ < 0.0016873148.**
- The leading #1148 line sits on words whose caps are **0.17–0.21% below** the selected word's. Those words move local mass from rank 1 to rank 2 (5,590 against 5,584–5,586 per call). The line leads because it packs closer to its cap. Its gain is in realizability, not in a better paid profile.
- For reviewers: claims on the same word differ only in packing. A claim on a lower-cap word can never overtake the best packing of a higher-cap word. The largest remaining packing prize is about +0.7%, for packing W1 or W2 as tightly as the #1148 line packs its own words.

## Not covered
- 16 claims (#1104 #1107 #1111 #1117 #1121 #1150 #1154 #1169 #1172 #1175 #1176 #1183 #1192 #1201 #1207 #1218) do not record a profile matching the title κ together with an idle histogram in one package. They are listed in `SNAPSHOT.json`.
- #1172's head moved during the snapshot, and the fetched head was used.
- Caps are planning bounds (`κ < a/(1+a)`). They allow fractional counts and ignore helper widths, windows and chronology.

## Reproduce
```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-queue-ceiling-census/verify.py           # ~12 s
python3 -I -B research/complex-queue-ceiling-census/rebind.py --fetch   # re-binds all 14 blobs
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-queue-ceiling-census
```
